# Write and Organize

Write prose in `.qmd` files using Markdown with Quarto extensions. Quarto adds
book structure, citations, cross-references, mathematics, and publishing
formats while keeping the source readable as plain text [@quarto-guide].

## Add chapters

Create the next numbered chapter without editing a separate contents file:

```sh
make chapter TITLE="From Relays to Transistors"
```

The command creates a file such as
`manuscript/chapters/06-from-relays-to-transistors.qmd`. Chapter filenames must
use `NN-kebab-case.qmd`; their numeric prefixes determine book order.

You may rename the starter `01-first-chapter.qmd` once you choose a real title.
Keep the numeric prefix and update `[excerpt].chapters` in `book.toml` if the
renamed file is part of the public excerpt.

Add appendices in the same way by creating numbered `.qmd` files under
`manuscript/appendices/`. They appear after the chapters automatically.

## Structure a chapter

Use one level-one heading for the chapter and level-two headings for its main
sections:

```markdown
# From Relays to Transistors

Opening prose introduces the chapter.

## Electromechanical switching

Section prose goes here.

### Contact bounce

Use deeper headings only when they make navigation clearer.
```

Give an important destination an explicit identifier, then refer to it by ID:

```markdown
## Contact bounce {#sec-contact-bounce}

As explained in @sec-contact-bounce, the contacts do not settle instantly.
```

Explicit IDs survive wording changes and make links more durable. Prefer them
for sections, figures, tables, equations, listings, exercises, and other items
you expect to reference.

## Keep the source portable

Use semantic Markdown before raw HTML or Typst. A few dependable forms
cover most prose:

- `**bold**` for strong importance and `*italic*` for emphasis;
- `` `inline code` `` for commands, filenames, and identifiers;
- `[useful link text](https://example.com)` for links;
- `[^reason]` for a named footnote reference; and
- block quotes beginning with `>` for quoted prose.

A plain named footnote needs no registry.[^native-footnote]

[^native-footnote]: Native named footnotes stay simple and portable.

Avoid using bold text as a substitute for headings, and never use color or an
icon as the only way to communicate meaning. These habits improve navigation,
EPUB reflow, and accessibility across every output.
